title: Regulating Imposition of Credit Card Fees by Banks
what_it_is: Regulating Imposition of Credit Card Fees by Banks

sections.label: MAS credit card fee disclosure
sections.summary: MAS requires banks to disclose late payment fees and interest charges, and ABS's Code specifies communication of principal terms and conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS does not interfere in these decisions, but expects all banks to deal fairly with their customers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In this regard, MAS requires banks to clearly and conspicuously disclose late payment fees and interest charges in credit card statements, including how such charges are computed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Where a customer has not paid the prior month’s credit card bill in full, the bank is required to provide in the current month’s statement a projection of the length of time and the total amount, including principal, interest, fees and charges, that the customer will take to fully pay off the entire outstanding balance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Association of Banks in Singapore’s Code of Consumer Banking Practice further specifies when and how banks can effectively communicate to customers, relevant information on a broader range of principal terms and conditions, including annual fees, repayment grace periods and interest rates.

sections.label: Regulating credit card annual fees
sections.summary: A question asks whether MAS can regulate credit card annual fees so those genuinely needing a card avoid paying them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This also means that if the consumer is not savvy enough, then they will have to pay for the credit card fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, my question to the Minister of State is whether MAS can regulate the imposition of this annual fee by the credit card companies so that those who genuinely need a credit card do not have to pay the annual fee.

sections.label: Fee waiver criteria and terms
sections.summary: Consumers can call in to an automated service, but fee waivers differ across products and issuers, so consumers should note terms and conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I think there are a few new initiatives where you can also call in and there is an automated service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: However, consumers also must be mindful that not all fee waivers will always be granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The criteria for these kinds of waivers, of course, differ across credit card products as well as issuers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, before taking up or signing up for a credit card, consumers should take note of the relevant terms and conditions, such as the expiry period of guaranteed fee waivers and the quantum of fees that are chargeable.
